analysis:
This batch is documentation only: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/ssd-eviction-selection.md, lines 1-13) and an addition to docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (a 2026-10-28 date bump at line 3, plus a paragraph inserted after line 530). No source code is supplied, so the implementation in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift and SSDBlockIndex.swift was not examined.

The documented behavior concerns the SSD prefix-cache eviction path, which relates to T-041 and asset A-001. The documented behavior is:
- It tries a linear `oldest` probe first.
- It falls back to a heap-based `oldestFirstSnapshot` only when the probe is busy or undeletable.
- The pass stays bounded.
- File leases, epoch validation, the removal lock and reconciliation back to the disk budget are retained.
- A closed store ends the pass.

The docs do not claim any change to the T-041 controls: HMAC lookup tags, AES-GCM, the 30-minute TTL, KEK purge, and per-file epoch behavior. LRU order is preserved for stable inputs. The docs note that concurrent schedules may pick different victims, which only affects which entry is evicted, not confidentiality.

The docs do not widen the at-rest surface or change TTL or scope. No security regression or threat-model gap is identifiable from the text.

Remaining questions for the code pass, if one is in scope:
- Whether the snapshot copy of the index holds HMAC tags only and never persists them.
- Whether early termination on a closed store leaves the disk budget unmet under pressure, which would be an availability concern (T-016).
- Whether the snapshot excludes the first tag correctly.

These are unverified because the code is absent. The docs excerpt at line 550 is truncated in the patch, but the base and head text cover the changed region.
